name_reason: The descriptor portion is correct and meaningful: disassembly at 0x101b9 (PUSH 0x50023; JMP to the printf/exit tail at 0x10056) confirms this literal is the OOM message printed when malloc(0x8a3) for the tile_event_data_table (stored to _data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr @ 0x53a55) fails inside fd2_load_save_and_init_engine. The 'save_load' domain and 'string'/'oom_msg' type tags are correct. The trailing '_50023' equals the symbol's own address (0x50023) and is pure Ghidra address residue per the naming rule, so it should be dropped. Disambiguation from the byte-identical sibling OOM strings in the same function is already provided by the descriptors (load_pbuf / tile_event / runtime_char), so the address suffix is redundant. NOTE: the three siblings (0x50004 _load_pbuf_50004, 0x50037 _runtime_char_50037) share the same address-residue suffix pattern and should be renamed as a consistent set in Stage 2 (each descriptor uniquely disambiguates without the address).
purpose: Read-only ASCII C string " Out of Memory !!!\n" (with NUL, 20 bytes) printed by fd2_load_save_and_init_engine when the tile_event_data_table malloc(0x8a3) allocation fails, just before the program exits.
logic_summary: Stored as an explicit 20-byte NUL-terminated literal, byte-exact with FD2.LE. In the LOAD-GAME path of fd2_load_save_and_init_engine, after malloc(0x8a3) for _data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr returns NULL, the code sets the keyboard/last-key flag to 3, issues int386(0x10,...) to reset BIOS text mode, loads &this[0] (PUSH 0x50023) and falls through to printf(msg) then exit(1). One DATA xref, from 0x101b9 in fd2_load_save_and_init_engine. Byte-identical to three other OOM copies (0x50004, 0x50037 in the same function; 0x50064 in fd2_load_chapter_battle_data) but a separate literal storage.
element_semantics: char bytes of the message " Out of Memory !!!\n" followed by a terminating NUL; consumed whole as a char* by printf, indexed by the CRT printf only.
comment_original_issue: Existing src comment was accurate and concise but omitted the BIOS int 10h text-mode reset that precedes the printf on this OOM path (the 0x50004 sibling comment already mentions it) and did not cross-reference both sibling OOM copies in the same function.
